The sibling predictors are reported too. The paper line 'S_adj is mildly informative in about half the groups and is not a confirmed predictor' is the right size. Nothing here narrows the paper.
  > 
  > **One sentence to change.** Rev. 14 says the non-identification account 'predicts exactly this' (a data-computable score helps only where the corner is partly identified). The account was formulated after P5(ii) failed, and it would be compatible with a clean pass (the score identifies the corner somewhere), a null result, and a mixed one. A mixed result with the gain concentrated in (d) is one outcome it allows, not one it singled out in advance. Please write 'is consistent with' instead, and keep the clause you already have that P7 does not confirm the account. P6(2) and the controls remain its test.
  > 
  > **For the P6 block, when it lands** (no action now): read B₂ as conservative, as rev. 13 says; the discriminating results are κ* net of κ*₀, C2/C3/C3′, the tails, and the oracle width ratio. On the HK-versus-BA/WS check you asked analysis for: the HK block has one degree-tail-plus-clustering setting per cell, so a match to the real graphs would support the two-factor reading only weakly; label it as such.
